about: The second reading of the translations (package S-19), one record per language: what was changed because it was clearly wrong, and the places a native speaker should decide. `npm run translations:export` puts the questions at the top of <lang>.md and in the first rows of <lang>.csv. Czech keys are written with ordinary spaces.

fixed.why: The name of the savings part. As a noun, „ja” is neuter (moje ja), and the other texts already decline it so (przyszłego ja, przyszłemu ja).

fixed.cs: Kolik šlo do „Budoucí já" (spoření a investice)?
fixed.before: Ile poszło na „Przyszłą mnie" (oszczędności i inwestycje)?
fixed.after: Ile poszło na „Przyszłe ja" (oszczędności i inwestycje)?
fixed.why: The question quotes the part's name, so it now uses the same name.

check.question: „przyszłemu sobie” is masculine. The part is called „Przyszłe ja”: would „Najpierw zapłać swojemu przyszłemu ja” sound natural, or is „zapłać najpierw sobie” the phrase people know?

check.question: Where Czech has to choose, the Czech source speaks to a woman (also „Věděla jsi?” and the reflection questions in the first person), and Polish follows it (czułaś, odłożyłam). Does that read naturally, or should these texts be neutral?

check.question: This text and one other write „20%”; fifteen others write „100 %” with a space, as Czech does. Which is right in Polish, so all can follow it?

check.question: Where Czech has to choose, the Czech source speaks to a woman (also „Jak ses cítila” and the reflection questions in the first person), and Ukrainian follows it (знала, відклала). Does that read naturally, or should these texts be neutral?
Would Ukrainian teachers and trainers say „воркшоп”, or rather „майстер-клас” or „семінар”?
Is „ведучий” the usual word for the person leading a workshop, or „фасилітатор” or „тренер”?

check.cs: Co z příběhu platí i pro vás?
check.question: The questions for a group use vosotros (Spain). Groups in Latin America would need ustedes. Keep vosotros?
„Tranquila” is feminine, following the Czech question „Jak ses cítila”. Would a neutral answer (for example „Con calma: los había pensado”) read better?
Deleting one item says „Eliminar”, deleting data or a workshop „Borrar”. Is that the usual split?
